# Jubilees Chapter 11 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abraham's Youth; Idolatry in Ur; Abraham's Early Righteousness

---

**11:1** In the thirty-fifth jubilee, in the third week, in the first year thereof, Reu took a wife named 'Ora, daughter of 'Ur son of Kesed. She bore him a son, and he named him Sarugh in the seventh year of that week.

**11:2** The sons of Noah began to make war on one another — taking captives, killing one another, and shedding human blood on the earth. They ate blood. They built fortified cities, walls, and towers. Individuals began to exalt themselves over their nations and to establish the beginnings of kingdoms. Nation made war against nation, city against city, and all began to pursue evil — acquiring weapons, teaching their sons warfare, seizing cities, and trading in male and female slaves.

**11:3** Mastema sent ravens and birds to devour the seed sown in the land, to destroy the land and rob the children of men of their labor. Before they could plow in the seed, the ravens picked it from the surface of the ground.

**11:4** For this reason he named him Reu: for the time was evil, and they were devouring one another.

**11:5** Sarugh took a wife named Melka, daughter of Kaber, daughter of his father's brother, in the thirty-sixth jubilee, in the fifth week, in the first year thereof.

**11:6** She bore him Nahor in the first year of the third week. Nahor grew up and lived in Ur of the Chaldees, and his father taught him the studies of the Chaldeans — to divine and practice augury according to the signs of heaven.

**11:7** In the thirty-seventh jubilee, in the sixth week, in the first year thereof, Nahor took a wife named 'Ijaska, daughter of Nestag of the Chaldees.

**11:8** She bore him Terah in the seventh year of that week.

**11:9** The prince Mastema sent ravens and birds to devour the seed before it was plowed in, and they were destroying all the work of the children of men. And he sent a destroying angel among them.

**11:10** In the thirty-ninth jubilee, in the second week, in the first year thereof, Terah took a wife named 'Edna', daughter of 'Abram, daughter of his father's brother.

**11:11** She bore him a son in the seventh year of that week, and he named him Abram, after the name of his mother's father, who had died before his daughter bore a son.

**11:12** The child began to perceive the errors of the earth — that everyone was going astray after carved images and after impurity — and his father taught him writing.

**11:13** He sought and understood the judgment of God, and separated himself from his father, refusing to worship idols alongside him.

**11:14** He prayed to God to have mercy on him and deliver him from the errors of humanity, so that his lot would not fall in the defilement of idolatry.

**11:15** Sowing time came, and everyone went out together to protect their seed from the ravens, for in those days all the ravens and kites devoured the sown seed.

**11:16** Abram went out in the morning to guard the seed, and a flock of ravens came to eat it.

**11:17** He ran toward them before they could land on the ground and called out to them: "Do not come down! Return to where you came from!" And they turned back.

**11:18** That day he drove them away seventy times, and not one settled on any of his father's fields.

**11:19** He remembered that day and wrote it down as a memorial.

**11:20** As the sun set his father called him, sat him down beside him, and said: "My son, what wonderful things you did today! Truly you are born to be mine."

**11:21** Abram told his father everything, saying: "Because of the devastation the ravens bring to the whole land, I protected our seed."

**11:22** His father rejoiced greatly, and Abram rose in his father's esteem.

**11:23** Terah his father said to him: "So it will be with your descendants all their days — the ravens will not devour their seed."

**11:24** In the sixtieth year of Abram's life — in the fourth week, in the fourth year thereof — Abram rose at night and burned the house of the idols. He burned everything that was in the house.

**11:25** He burned all of it, and no man knew. They arose in the night and tried to save their gods from the fire.

**11:26** Haran rushed to save them, but the fire blazed over him and burned him, and he died in Ur of the Chaldees before his father Terah; and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldees.

**11:27** Terah went out from Ur of the Chaldees — he and his sons — to go to the land of Lebanon and the land of Canaan. He settled in the land of Haran, and Abram lived with his father in Haran for two weeks of years.

---
*LOGOS notes: Abram's anti-idolatry exploits (vv.12-26) — especially the bird-chasing (vv.15-19) and the burning of the idol-house (vv.24-26) — are Jubilees-unique. The idol-burning with Haran's death parallels rabbinic legend (Genesis Rabbah 38:13). The chronological precision ("sixtieth year," v.24) reflects Jubilees' dating system.*
